content: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are considered the first-line therapeutic agents for managing hypertension in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly in those who exhibit significant levels of albuminuria. These medications are effective in lowering albuminuria levels, achieving better blood pressure control, and decelerating the progression of CKD. For individuals with severe albuminuria, defined as urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) ≥ 300 mg/g, the use of ACE inhibitors or ARBs has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD). However, to maximize their therapeutic benefits, these agents should be administered at the highest doses that the patient can tolerate without adverse effects.
